title: Champlain Towers South: open NCST investigation, pool-deck/tower hypotheses, records/QC/QA questions
summary: Champlain Towers South is encoded as an open-investigation structural-failure record with strict preliminary-status guardrails: NIST sources point toward pool-deck and slab-column/corrosion/construction/records questions, but final cause is not yet settled in this cube.

subjects.name: NIST National Construction Safety Team investigation

claims.claim: NIST records that Champlain Towers South partially collapsed on June 24, 2021, and that NIST deployed a team the next day to collect information and preserve materials and evidence.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: NIST’s September 2025 update says the collapse likely started in the pool deck rather than the tower, notes visible distress weeks before collapse, and identifies pool-deck slab-column connection, corrosion, shrinkage, and improperly built joint questions as focus areas.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: NIST’s June 2025 update frames preliminary hypothesis likelihood, including corrosion, reinforcement placement, water exposure, and lower-likelihood karst/pile hypotheses, while making clear the investigation is still using evidence and analysis rather than a final report.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: NIST’s June 2025 and March 2026 updates preserve the correction-memory questions future records should track: records retention, quality control/assurance, timeline, testing, and a final report expected later rather than already complete.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: This cube must treat Champlain as an open/preliminary structural-failure record, not a final-cause record; the claim status should change when NIST issues the final report or materially updates the technical findings.

type_payload.incident_class: occupied building partial collapse under active federal investigation

sequence_of_events.event: Champlain Towers South partially collapsed in June 2021.
NIST deployed and began NCST-style evidence collection and analysis.
NIST public updates identified pool-deck initiation as likely and narrowed several higher/lower likelihood hypotheses.
Final report and definitive causal status remain pending in this cube.

latent_conditions: records retention and construction/inspection documentation may affect post-collapse legibility
visible distress and maintenance/repair decision surfaces require final-report extraction before stronger claims
high public consequence makes premature causal certainty especially dangerous

handling_notes: Preserve dignity of victims, families, responders, engineers, inspectors, and occupants; avoid casualty spectacle.
Use official investigation language to understand system conditions, not to assign unsourced individual blame.
Record source boundaries and avoid overgeneralizing from one structural system to all structures.
